comment: Vreta's mood, applied by Unity's golfmap.look.apply. Found live in GSPro 2026-10-13 against the reference courses (docs/gspro/reference-courses.md): they all run a dark ambient ground (0.08-0.17; Vreta had 0.50, which lit crowns and forest floor from below and flattened them) and colour grading saturation about -30 (Vreta had -0.7, the reason grass, bilberry and bushes each looked candy-green). Before: ambient sky #b8adb4, equator #adc4a9, ground #807d75; saturation -0.7, postExposure 2.6, AO colour #48786f. Second pass the same day (screenshots tree-export/arborist-shots/day3/look, L0 = before, L5 = these values): GSPRO READS THE POST-PROCESSING FROM THE COURSE FOLDER'S arborist_postprocess.dat, NOT FROM THE SCENE'S PROFILE, so until that file is exported again (Unity Tools > Arborist Postprocessing, after golfmap.look.apply) or removed, nothing under 'post' reaches GSPro; ambient, sun and fog come from the scene. sun.shadowStrength 0.556 -> 0.8: shadows under the trees read as shadows; 0.95 took the forest floor to 29 % near-black pixels. post.aoIntensity 1.29 -> 0.6: multi-scale AO at 1.29 darkened every leaf card and the whole forest floor, not only contacts (floor luma 48 without AO, 40 at 0.6, 33 at 1.29). post.liftW -0.03 is what the .dat held; the Unity profile's -0.2068 makes shaded vegetation black (floor: 56 % near-black pixels against 26 %). post.saturation stays -18: grass is then at 38-45 % saturation (46-56 % before), not grey; -30 takes fairways to 24-26 % and reads olive-grey. post.bloom is unchanged on purpose: Vreta's sky is brighter than CE's (skybox exposure 1 against 0.58-0.77), so threshold 0.25 at intensity 3 washes the crowns against the sky grey (chroma 27 -> 17) and whitens the far wall; 0.9 does nothing visible. fog was start 150, end 1000, intensity 2.6 with OPCD's default gradient, which turned everything beyond 300 m cyan-grey; start 0, end 2500, intensity 2.0 kept the far wall the colour of the near trees and only a little lighter, but hazed the near trees grey too and left the billboard wall olive-brown (hue 60-67). 2026-10-14 (Marcus): start 150, end 1000, intensity 2.0 - the first 150 m clear, the horizon blue-green and lighter (far band hue 84 -> 98, lightness 0.37 -> 0.41, measured in GSPro), which hides where billboards do not quite match their models; a little haze is fine on a June morning. The fog's tint is the gradient texture on the GradientFog object and is not set here. Third pass the same day, to Marcus's brief (a fine summer day, 10:00, late June in Sweden, lush green starting to dry a little; he found the second pass too cold): sun.elevation 43 / azimuth 119 is the sun at that hour at 58.5 N 15.5 E (the scene had 34 degrees from west-north-west, an evening sun); post.temperature 13.5 -> 22 gives the grass its yellow-green back with the sky still blue (30 yellows the sky; pulling the blue mixer down instead turned it murky); sky.exposure 1 -> 0.7 (Marcus liked 0.75 and 0.65 both and chose the middle) makes the sky blue instead of near white at the horizon and gives the clouds form (the forest references run 0.58-0.77). Tried live together, tree-export/arborist-shots/day3/look/JUNE-compare-*.png. AO radius is not a key: the profile runs MultiScaleVolumetricObscurance, which has no radius. 2026-10-16: Omberg's new scene came out much paler than Vreta because these were not in the look yet and came from its template: sun.intensity (1.3 there), the skybox (BlueSky_Bright, tint 0.88) and the reflection intensity (0), and the profile's contrast / lift / gamma / gain (v4_Sunny_Pop: gain w +0.05, gamma w +0.03, contrast 18). They are keys now, at Vreta's values: sun.intensity, sun.clock (OPCD's TimeAdjust, which look.apply switches off; GSPro keeps the saved direction), sky.material (a project skybox by name), sky.reflectionIntensity, post.contrast and post.lift / gamma / gain as [x, y, z, w]. GSPro still takes the post values from arborist_postprocess.dat.
